## Preamble

This script runs GO Enrichment using `topGo` on our `DESeq2` analysis results. This script is adapted from the Lecture 7.3 script provided by MICB 405 at the University of British Columbia Vancouver (2026W1).

## 1. Load Libraries

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(topGO))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
```

## 2. Generate Gene Universe

```{r}
# Create Mapping Table
geneID2GO <- readMappings("go_term_tables/mesaur_GOIDs.tsv")

# Generate `topGO` Gene Universe
geneUniverse <- names(geneID2GO)

```

## 3. Load Lists of Differentially Expressed Genes

```{r}
# Load raw gene lists
up_gene <- read.csv("deseq2_results/top_dpi_diff_expressed.csv")
down_gene <- read.csv("deseq2_results/bot_dpi_diff_expressed.csv")

# Convert/Coerce to characters
upregulated_gene_names <- as.character(up_gene$gene_id)
downregulated_gene_names <- as.character(down_gene$gene_id)

# Convert to factors
up_gene_list <- factor(as.integer(geneUniverse %in% upregulated_gene_names))
down_gene_list <- factor(as.integer(geneUniverse %in% downregulated_gene_names))
names(up_gene_list) <- geneUniverse
names(down_gene_list) <- geneUniverse
```

## 4. Build topGOdata Objects

```{r}
# up-regulated genes
up_GO_data <- new("topGOdata",
                  description = "mesaur_4dpi_80_dpi_mock_cov",
                  ontology = "BP",
                  allGenes = up_gene_list,
                  annot = annFUN.gene2GO,
                  gene2GO = geneID2GO)

# down-regulated genes
down_GO_data <- new("topGOdata",
                    description = "mesaur_4dpi_80_dpi_mock_cov",
                    ontology = "BP",
                    allGenes = down_gene_list,
                    annot = annFUN.gene2GO,
                    gene2GO = geneID2GO)

```

## 5. Run Statistical Tests on topGOdata Objects

```{r}
up_result <- runTest(up_GO_data,
                     algorithm = "weight01",
                     statistic = "fisher")

down_result <- runTest(down_GO_data,
                       algorithm = "weight01",
                       statistic = "fisher")
```

Now we can finally extract our results. You can change the number of results you want reported with the `topNodes` parameter.

```{r}
# Extract a summary of upregulated results
up_GO <- GenTable(up_GO_data,
                       weight01 = up_result,
                       orderBy = "weight01",
                       ranksOf = "weight01",
                       topNodes = 50)

# Extract a summary of downregulated results
down_GO <- GenTable(down_GO_data,
                         weight01 = down_result,
                         orderBy = "weight01",
                         ranksOf = "weight01",
                         topNodes = 50)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<br></br>

# Visualizing topGO Analyses

Finally, we can actually try and visualize our results!

Let's visualize the data by plotting the enrichment ratio for every GO annotation. The enrichment ratio refers to how many of the annotated genes aligned to a specific GO term were significantly upregulated/downregulated. We will filter out any statistically insignificant entries, manually calculate the GeneRatio (simply the number of Significant GO annotations vs Annotated).

```{r}
# Filter out any non-significant data and calculate the gene ratio
down_GO_filtered <- down_GO %>%
  mutate(GeneRatio = Significant/Annotated, weight01 = as.numeric(weight01)) %>%
  filter(weight01 <= 0.05) %>%
  head(n = 20)
```

<br></br>

Let's plot some of the GO terms we found were enriched in our downregulated genes. We'll make a dotplot and add thin bars with `geom_col()` that follow the dot, which is an aesthetic choice.

```{r}
down_GO_filtered %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Term, y = GeneRatio)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.05) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  coord_flip() # Flip the axes so the x-axis labels are readable
```

<br></br>

Now let's add another layer to this plot! We can make it such that the colour of the points and 'lines' represent the p-value (weight01). We will also order our plot based on enrichment ratio. To do this, we'll need to rearrange our data and convert the `Term` variable to a factor to actually reorder.

```{r}
# First, let's arrange the data based on the enrichment ratio. 
down_GO_filtered_arranged <- down_GO_filtered %>% 
  arrange(GeneRatio) %>%
  mutate(Term = factor(Term))

# Now let's extract the order of the term column
order_term <- down_GO_filtered_arranged %>% 
  pull(Term) # pull() extracts a column as a vector
```

<br></br>

Let's see what the plot looks like. Here, `scale_x_discrete(limits = )` will reorder the graph based on the order of the vector we provide it. We'll use `scale_colour_gradient()` to specify how we want the colour to change.

```{r}
down_GO_filtered_arranged %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x= Term, y = GeneRatio, fill = weight01)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.05) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = order_term) + 
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue")
```

<br></br>

We can now see that those genes in red are more significant than the ones in blue. Finally, let's add our last change to this plot. Let's make it such that the size of the points in the plot is proportional to the number of significantly downregulated genes in that gene set. Since we want to have the size of points in `geom_point` scale with the number of Significant genes in a GO term, the size of point now ***depends*** on our data. This means we have to specify it in an `aesthetic()`. Since we only want the size of points to change and nothing else, we'll specify the `aesthetic()` within `geom_point()`.

```{r}
down_GO_filtered_arranged %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x= Term, y = GeneRatio, color = weight01)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.05) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Significant)) + 
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = order_term) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue") +
  
  # Add these to make our plot prettier
  theme_light() +
  labs(x = "GO Term Description", y = "Enrichment Ratio", color = "weight01 p-value", size = "Number of Significant Genes") + 
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"), panel.grid = element_line(colour = "grey96")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = c(0, 0)) # this changes the scale of the axes
```

<br></br>

And as always, you can do the same type of analysis with the upregulated genes!

Here is a cool graph that contains both upregulated and downregulated genes. The steps are all essentially the same, but with two added caveats. I've add labels and concatenated the upregulated and downregulated dataframes. I've also added an extra command in the plot (`facet_grid()`) that splits the data based on a column of data. Give this a try with your data!

```{r plot-updown, warning=FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Add labels to upregulated and downregulated dataframes
up_GO <- up_GO %>% 
  mutate(up_down = "UP")

down_GO <- down_GO %>% 
  mutate(up_down = "DOWN")

# Make a joined dataframe
joined_GO_filtered_arranged <- bind_rows(up_GO, down_GO) %>%
  mutate(GeneRatio = Significant/Annotated, weight01 = as.numeric(weight01)) %>%
  filter(weight01 <= 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(GeneRatio)) %>%
  mutate(Term = factor(Term)) %>%
  head(n = 40)

# Extract the column order
order_term_joined <- joined_GO_filtered_arranged %>% 
  pull(Term)

joined_GO_filtered_arranged %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x= Term, y = GeneRatio, color = weight01)) +
  geom_point(aes(size= Significant)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = order_term_joined) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "red", high = "blue") +
  theme_light() +
  labs(x = "GO Term Description", y = "Enrichment Ratio", color = "weight01 p-value", size = "Number of Significant Genes") +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"), 
        panel.grid = element_line(colour = "grey96"), 
        strip.background = element_rect(colour = "black")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  facet_grid(.~ up_down)
```

<br></br>

Finally, we can also extract a GO term that was highly enriched and find all the genes that were mapped to it. You might do this if you're interested in how gene expression changes for genes associated with a certain GO ID. To do this, we will use the `chlamy_GOIDs.tsv` file. We'll reload this file into our workspace as a dataframe

```{r message=FALSE}
# load the tsv file
chlamy_GOIDs <- read_tsv("data/chlamy_GOIDs.tsv", col_names = c("gene_id", "GO_id"))
glimpse(chlamy_GOIDs)
```

<br></br>

First, choose a GO ID from our downregulated data set. I'll arbitrarily choose the GO ID from the 20th row.

```{r}
GO_ID <- down_GO_filtered_arranged$GO.ID[20]
```

<br></br>

Now let's use this to pull the rows that contain that ID. Since our `GO_id` column is a string containing multiple GO IDs, we can't just filter the column for the specific GO ID. Instead, we can filter with `grepl` (yes, this is basically the same as grep). `grepl` will look in a string for a specific pattern and return TRUE or FALSE depending on if the pattern exists.

```{r}
# Select rows that contain our GO term of interest
filtered_GO_ID <- chlamy_GOIDs %>%
  filter(grepl(pattern = GO_ID, GO_id))
glimpse(filtered_GO_ID)
```

<br></br>

Now we'll select the genes in our differential expression data that contain our GO ID of interest.

```{r}
# Vector of gene IDs to select
gene_id_vector <- filtered_GO_ID %>% 
  pull(gene_id)

# Filter the data set
dat_GO_filtered <- data %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% gene_id_vector) %>%
  filter(padj <= 0.05 & log2FoldChange <= -1)

glimpse(dat_GO_filtered)
```

<br></br>

Now you could play around with the data for the specific GO term! For example:

```{r}
dat_GO_filtered %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gene_id, y = log2FoldChange)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = log2FoldChange - lfcSE, ymax =log2FoldChange + lfcSE), width = 0.4) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.8) +
  coord_flip()+ 
  labs(y = "log2(FC)", x= "Gene ID") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"), panel.grid = element_line(colour = "white"))
```
